newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ACCC to decide Westpac deal in 3, 4 weeks.
newsitem.headline: ACCC to decide Westpac deal in 3, 4 weeks.

text.p: The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), the national monopolies watchdog, will take at least three or four weeks to determine Westpac Banking Corp's proposed takeover of Bank of Melbourne Ltd, a spokeswoman said on Wednesday.
"It will be at least three or four weeks," she told Reuters.
"It (the determination) would not be before May."
Westpac announced last week a A$1.435 billion friendly bid for Bank of Melbourne, which operates in the state of Victoria.
The commission can veto business deals that inhibit competition and Treasurer Peter Costello has an additional power to veto bank acquisitions and mergers.

Costello said earlier on Tuesday that he would be guided in the exercise of his discretion by the commission's guidelines that have previously blocked mergers that would eliminate the last big regional bank in a state.
He did not, however, say whether that meant he would simply confirm the commission's decision.
The spokeswoman said the commission was still waiting for submissions from the two banks.
